caseStudy.title: QuaySignals
caseStudy.background:
QuaySignals runs a Container Apps gateway in multiple revision mode with an AKS embedding service downstream. The next release adds an optional formatting capability behind App Configuration. The team has been asked to diagnose a failed canary without changing cluster-wide settings.

The release dashboard shows the candidate has Ready Pods but no Service endpoints. An AKS manifest was edited to use a different application label. Pgvector retrieval after the rollout uses HNSW and applies a selective site filter. It now returns fewer than the requested 20 results even though at least 100 eligible records exist.

The gateway accepts documents through Service Bus with duplicate detection enabled. Support wants components to share one trace graph without recording document contents.

questions.explanation: Group by role and binned timestamps. Grouping by raw timestamps or role only omits the requested interval grouping.
options: summarize Failures=count() by AppRoleName
summarize Failures=count() by AppRoleName, TimeGenerated
project AppRoleName, bin(TimeGenerated, 12m)
summarize Failures=count() by AppRoleName, bin(TimeGenerated, 12m)

questions.prompt: The north deployment has 226 usable database connections, 11 steady replicas and maxSurge 3. What is the maximum equal per-Pod connection pool size that respects the rollout budget?
questions.explanation: During rollout up to replicas plus surge Pods can coexist. Divide the usable connections by that maximum and round down.

questions.prompt: The team replaces the embedding index while preserving reads during backfill. The database contains 200,000 writable rows. What rollout keeps the search and source update paths consistent?
questions.answer: Backfill a versioned index, make live writes update the new version, validate, then switch readers through a controlled cutover
questions.explanation: Backfill plus coverage for ongoing writes avoids a synchronization gap. A versioned cutover retains rollback.
options: Update the existing index in place and change the encoder before validation
Export a single vector ranking and treat it as valid for both models
Switch readers to the empty candidate and rewrite old records from their summaries
Backfill a versioned index, make live writes update the new version, validate, then switch readers through a controlled cutover

questions.prompt: Cosmos DB commits a new document, then the API exits before publishing a Service Bus message. Which design ensures a retryable publication signal without an unsafe dual-write assumption?
questions.answer: Record the document and an outbox item under the same Cosmos logical partition in a transactional batch, then publish via change feed with stable IDs
questions.explanation: Cosmos transactional batches are atomic within a logical partition. A change-feed publisher can retry durable outbox records.
options: Use separate logical partitions and assume Cosmos transactions span both
Write the document and publish separately, treating the first success as proof of both
Dispatch the message first and assume subscribers can always find the document
Record the document and an outbox item under the same Cosmos logical partition in a transactional batch, then publish via change feed with stable IDs
